source.quote: the 8B model is trained with a maximum context length of 8K, while the 32B model is trained with a maximum context length of 128K.
We introduce the Aya Expanse, a family of multilingual instruction-tuned language models that support 23 languages

languages.value: 23 languages: Arabic, Chinese (simplified & traditional), Czech, Dutch, English, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Turkish, Ukrainian and Vietnamese

source.quote: These 23 languages are: Arabic, Chinese (simplified & traditional), Czech, Dutch, English, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Turkish, Ukrainian and Vietnamese.
the Aya Expanse models are an open-weights release of both 8-billion and 32-billion parameters

architecture.value: SwiGLU activation, RoPE positional embeddings, grouped-query attention; based on Cohere Command series

source.quote: both 8B and 32B models use SwiGLU activation function [Shazeer, 2020], RoPE positional embeddings [Su et al., 2021] and grouped-query attention [Ainslie et al., 2023].

trainingData.value: Command-series pretraining on a 23-language text mixture; post-training via multilingual data arbitrage, offline then online iterative DPO preference training, and model merging

source.quote: which are pre-trained using a data mixture that includes texts from 23 languages.

findings.text: During online iterative direct preference optimization (DPO), going beyond 3 iterations sometimes introduced reward hacking behavior, so both models stopped at 3 iterations.

source.quote: we repeat this process for 3 iterations as we found that going beyond 3 iterations led to minimal gains at the cost of additional re-tuning parameters like regularization coefficient (β) and sometimes introduced reward hacking behavior.

notes: Technical report (not a system card); no dedicated safety section and no safety/alignment/jailbreak/bias/toxicity eval numbers. Mentions of multilingual preference optimization and safety tuning cite prior papers (Dang et al. 2024; Aakanksha et al. 2024a) as training methods, not results for Aya Expanse—so topics stay uncovered. Skipped all capability evals (m-ArenaHard, Dolly win-rates, Global-MMLU, INCLUDE, XWinograd, XCOPA, XStoryCloze, MGSM, FLORES). Preprint date December 6, 2024 is not treated as a model releaseDate. Cohere For AI Community thanked for testing at release is not counted as an external safety tester.
